Champion:
'''Champions''' are special units in Monster Train 2. Champions are usually some of the strongest units available, though their role varies widely, with some based around dealing damage and others based around support or even permanently scaling your other units. Each clan has two Champions, one primary and one alternate. Primary Champions are available from the start, while alternate Champions are unlocked at level 5.

You will always have one Champion from your main clan, and do not get one from your allied clan. They cannot be duplicated outside of battle, and can only be permanently removed using [[Void Armament]] or by taking [[Shardsoul]].

Instead of being upgraded like other units, Champions each have a set of three upgrade paths, with three levels of each. Champions are upgraded at the [[Light Forge]].

Champions always cost {{Ember|0}}, unless the cost is increased through [[Savage Shackles]].

The bulkier train steward design is one of the results of her efforts.'' |artist = Nicole Anne Alfonso }} The '''Shield Steward''' is an common [[Clanless]] banner unit. Each run starts with two of them. It has no special abilities. == Strategy == '''Shield Steward''' can be a crucial tool for some decks to survive in Ring 1 and sometimes Ring 2, as you may not have another unit that can take damage well, and against the boss, you'll need one! Taking the [[Trials#Mark of Invasion|Mark of Invasion trial]] in Ring 1 can be incorrect if doing so involves '''Shield Steward''' taking too much damage by the time the boss arrives. If '''Shield Steward''' is on low health by then, you won't do well against the boss and on higher Covenants your run might end before it even started. If your deck is looking weak into the Ring 2 or 3 boss, it's often a good idea to put some cheap shop upgrades on a '''Shield Steward'''. Since you will usually throw this unit away eventually, a small {{Gold}} investment can ensure you actually survive until the late game, and unlike other banner units there's no opportunity cost in filling up its upgrade slots with comparatively weak minor upgrades. In particular, against the '''Pyre Hunter''' variant of [[Arkion]], a '''Shield Steward''' on the top floor with no upgrades will die the second time he flies up to the top floor and let him hit your Pyre, but with a {{IconLink|Heartstone}}, it will survive two rounds of being attacked. Additionally, if you activate [[Fleshweaver]]'s Titan Trial, all variants will have enough {{Attack}} to kill an unupgraded '''Shield Steward''' on the first turn. {{IconLink|Heartstone}} can help with this again, but against '''Spiked Mass''' you will also need a {{IconLink|Strengthstone}} or equivalent {{Attack}} boost for the '''Shield Steward''' to kill the {{Health|9}} Fleshling before it ascends to the Pyre. [[Steward's Quarters]], if you find it, can make this unit playable into the lategame, though you've frequently committed to a different strategy by the time you see this room. Otherwise, '''Shield Steward''' becomes irrelevant by ring 3 at the latest. Despite having decent {{Health}}, it rarely functions as a tank in the lategame because of its {{Capacity}}. Because it's a banner unit, if you have extra {{IconLink|Deployment Ember}} and a spare floor to play '''Shield Steward''', it can be a lower Purge priority than other cards like [[Spear Steward]], as you can simply play it out during Deployment and forget it. It can even be a diversion to flying bosses on turn 1 if placed on the top floor. Alternatively, with [[Judge's Scales]], it can be worth keeping in your deck so that you can discard it and potentially draw a more useful card during Deployment. Otherwise it should be Purged. In order to unlock [[Herzal's Horde]], you need to deal a certain amount of damage using Train Stewards. Despite having lower {{Attack}} than Spear Steward, '''Shield Steward''' is usually better for this task, simply because you can play it more reliably. Covenant Ranks:
'''Covenant Ranks''' are the difficulty system in Monster Train 2, going from the easiest difficulty at Covenant 0 to the hardest at Covenant 10. Only Covenant Ranks 0 and 1 are initially available, and the rest must be unlocked by beating each Covenant in ascending order. Covenant Ranks 1-9 and Covenant Rank 10 each have their own winstreak counter.

When the player beats the Titans on Covenant Rank 10, the credits will roll.  (This is entirely the same as the credits which can be viewed from the menu.)

==List==

'''Covenant 1''': Enemies are stronger. Add additional random cards to your starting deck.

'''Covenant 2''': Battles have additional enemies.

'''Covenant 3''': Merchant reroll costs are 50% higher and purge costs scale 50% faster.

'''Covenant 4''': Bosses have increased {{Attack}} and {{Health}}. Non-Flying Bosses have an additional mechanic.

'''Covenant 5''': Add two '''[[Vengeful Shard]]s''' to the starting deck.

'''Covenant 6''': One card per draft also adds a '''[[Calcified Ember]]'''.

'''Covenant 7''': There is no longer an empty wave before bosses.

'''Covenant 8''': Enemies are stronger.

'''Covenant 9''': Your Pyre takes '''30%''' damage at the start of the run.

'''Covenant 10''': Elite Chosen Enemies appear during Flying Boss Battles

'''Pyre of Dominion''' is one of the [[Pyre Hearts]] in Monster Train 2. It immediately removes all Train Stewards and [[starter cards]]. The player then drafts from the following packs, gaining two copies of each card:
* Primary clan uncommon pack
* Allied clan uncommon pack
* Primary clan unit banner
* Allied clan unit banner
The cards cannot be skipped.

Because this Pyre removes 10 Starter cards and 4 Train Stewards from your deck but only adds 8 new cards, it effectively reduces your deck size by 6.

==Strategy==

'''Pyre of Dominion''' is generally one of the strongest Pyres in the game. Its stats are below average, but replacing all of your starting cards more than makes up for its weaknesses elsewhere. Not only does it get rid of your worst cards, it also gives you your choice of stronger cards to replace them.

This means that you will usually not need to pick up more cards to win early battles, so you can focus on removing cards in order to whittle your deck down to a few very strong options.

With that said, a few [[Champion|Champions]], especially [[Baron Grael]], actually gain a significant benefit from their starting cards and may be better off using a different Pyre. However, even in these cases the '''Pyre of Dominion''' can still be effective with a good initial draft.

== Recommended Clans and Champions ==

The biggest factor to the viability of using a clan and champion with the Pyre of Dominion is whether the champion's paths are contingent on their starter. Several starters have little synergy with the champions themselves, and better yet, some have abilities and paths that are redundant with their starters.

* None of '''[[Talos]]'''' paths require [[Inspire (spell)|Inspire]] to work particularly well - there's no shortage of other cards or effects from the [[Banished]] that can stack {{IconLink|Valor}}, and her '''Battle Cleric''' path fully replicates the effect of using Inspire on her floor every turn.
* '''[[Lord Fenix]]'s''' paths for '''Overlord''' and '''Golden Crown''' do not have any particular synergy with [[Firestarter]], and his ability already provides a way to apply some {{IconLink|Pyregel}}, albeit inconsistently.
* Outside of arguably her '''Everbloom''' path, little about '''[[Madame Lionsmane]]'s''' paths synergize with [[Sporetouch]]. Even her '''Sporeslinger''' path innately allows her to apply {{IconLink|Decay}} without using her starter, and it's easily possible to draft an initial card that also applies the effect.
* '''[[Orechi]]''' doesn't have any requirement for [[Secret Ingredient]] - the closest would be his '''Mad Scientist''' path, which is only an {{IconLink|Incant}} trigger, and so doesn't strictly require the effects of the starter. the Pyre of Dominion draft makes it possible to start with much more impactful and reliable spells to trigger it, such as [[Surgical Strike]] or [[Acid Shower]].
* '''[[Herzal]]'s''' [[Smith]] is a fairly low impact starter card with an effect that doesn't particularly align to any of his paths.
* While [[Torch]] is a serviceable starter attack spell, The '''[[Hornbreaker Prince]]''' doesn't have any paths that would miss it. It's well possible to draft cards that work better with his paths like '''Wrathful''' by giving him more strength to reliably maintain its {{IconLink|Revenge}} and {{IconLink|Slay}} cycle.
* '''[[Wyldenten]]'s''' [[Rootseeds]] are a low-impact starter without any specific synergies with his paths. The closest is his '''Thornlord''' path, which even then supplies its own [[Sting|Stings]] with Needlebloom.
* Both '''[[Tethys Titansbane]]''' and '''[[Solgard the Martyr]]''' are champions saddled with poorly-performing starters, and paths that mainly use them as stop-gap triggers for their paths: 
** Tethys comes the closest to synergy with [[Frozen Lance]] using her '''Conduit''' path. However, the starter spell simply lacks the flexibility to merit its mechanics, and the initial draft will also make it likely to draw more powerful uncommon attack spells such as [[Icestorm]] and [[Ice Tornado]] that make much greater use of the path's {{IconLink|Conduit}}.
** Solgard's issue with [[Forgone Power]] is that all his paths require regular {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers to function. While Forgone Power is low-cost, it doesn't have an impactful effect and its random discard means that even in a hand filled with starters the number of triggers of it won't ever be consistent. With a starting hand-size of 5, it's very possible to draft 4-6 better alternatives you can reliably draw into.
* The '''[[Primordium]]'s''' paths work best with a powerful front unit for it to feed - preferably one with a {{IconLink|Gorge}} trigger. [[Plink]] is an inconsistent starter damage spell that doesn't do much to support this playstyle, and the effects of the Pyre of Dominion means that it's very likely you'll be able to draft up to five suitable units the Primordium could feed.

'''Graft''' units that die lose the '''Graft''' status effect for the rest of the combat. This means that if they are replayed (via {{IconLink|Endless}} or '''[[Reform]]'''), they no longer have the equipment attached to them.

==Strategy==

One of the main questions when seeing an alcove is what other nodes you should take before or after checking it. 

It is good to check shops before Alcoves, if only to see what upgrades are available. Having fully upgraded units makes many events more useful, so you may want to buy upgrades before checking the Alcove. However, it may be worth waiting to buy upgrades in case you get a unit like [[Dante the Dependable]], so that you can quickly upgrade him.

[[Pyre Remains]] should always be saved until ''after'' checking the Alcove in Ring 3, or in any ring if you have at least 51 {{PyreHealth}}, or if your {{PyreHealth}} is low enough that you will not have 51 even after taking the Remains. If the Remains would push you over {{PyreHealth|51|bold=f}} in Ring 4 or later, you will need to consider whether you care more about potentially missing out on the [[Looming Darkshard]] or the [[Unstable Shard]] when deciding what order to take the nodes in.

== Soul Savior ==
In [[Soul Savior]] mode, 2-3 Celestial Alcoves are guaranteed to spawn as major nodes on either side of the track. Event selection works similarly to standard play. In the [[Celestial Alcove#Event Selection|Event Selection]] table above, "Ring" corresponds to the number of battles completed-1. Celestial Alcoves can spawn before any battle, but the spawning rules simply "extend" backwards from Ring 3 or forwards from Ring 7:
* The [[Archus]] event cannot be obtained until completing 3 battles (the first region boss).
* All events that are listed as unobtainable on Ring 7 cannot be obtained after completing the sixth battle (the first battle of the third region).

In addition to its primary inventory, the Merchant of Arms offers two unique services: '''Merge Equipment''' and '''Deployable Upgrade'''.

=== Primary Inventory ===
The merchant's primary inventory offers a choice of three cards for purchase, which are always:
* A random uncommon or rare [[Equipment]] card.
* A random uncommon or rare [[Room]] card.
* A random rare Equipment or Room card.
Uncommon cards cost {{Gold|40}}, and rare cards cost {{Gold|90}}.

=== Merge Equipment ===
This service allows you to create '''Merged Equipment''' with two equipment cards. The resulting card has all of the effects of both inputs, and its {{Ember}} cost is the sum of the input {{Ember}} costs. It costs {{Gold|75}}.

=== Deployable Upgrade ===
This service adds the Deployable keyword to a room or equipment card of your choice, causing it to appear in your hand during the deployment phase. It costs {{Gold|75}} (or {{Gold|40}} with [[Herzal's Horde]]).

== Notes ==
* The Merchant of Arms is the only merchant where the [[Lifemother's Pyre]] duplication ability cannot be used.
* The Monster Train 1 clans have fewer rooms and equipment than their new counterparts, making it much more likely to get Clanless cards.
* Merchant of Arms and [[Armory]] are the only map nodes that allow reliably acquiring extra cards outside of combat. [[Unit Banner]]s only offer banner units and cannot appear after Ring 5, and only certain [[Celestial Alcove]] events offer extra cards.

'''Merchant of Magic''' is a map node and [[Merchants|merchant]] in Monster Train 2.

4-5 Merchants of Magic are present on the map:
* A Merchant of Magic is guaranteed on [[Ring 2]], accompanying a [[Unit Banner]].
* A Merchant of Magic is guaranteed on either [[Ring 3]] or [[Ring 4]].
* A Merchant of Magic is guaranteed on either [[Ring 5]] or [[Ring 6]].
* A Merchant of Magic is present on one or both of [[Ring 7]] and [[Ring 8]].

The merchant's primary inventory offers a choice of four upgrades for purchase. One is a minor Magic Power upgrade, one is a minor ember cost upgrade, and two are major upgrades.
